description: This course introduces students to the design and implementation of knowledge-based systems (KBS), focusing on rule-based systems, expert systems, and hybrid architectures. Topics include knowledge representation using semantic networks, frames, and ontologies; reasoning mechanisms such as forward and backward chaining; knowledge acquisition techniques like interviews and document analysis; and the use of Prolog for logic programming. Students will explore the integration of machine learning models with traditional KBS, including the use of OWL for ontology development and SPARQL for querying semantic web data. The course also covers knowledge management strategies, including knowledge storage, retrieval, and maintenance in databases like Neo4j and MongoDB. Additional topics include knowledge engineering processes, the role of natural language processing in KBS, and the evaluation of KBS performance using precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The course emphasizes the application of KBS in domains such as healthcare, finance, and cybersecurity.
